title: Mapper glossary
summary: Plain-language meanings of the geometry, material, and build terms used by the editor.
outcome: You can pick the right object or command when following a tool procedure.

sections.title: Objects and selections
paragraphs: Brush: a solid volume built from faces. A structural, detail, noncolliding, or clip classification changes its build role.
Face: one surface of a brush; Face mode lets you target its material and projection.
Vertex: an editable corner or control point. Vertex mode exposes handles for a selected brush, terrain, or curved patch.
Curved patch: a controlled curved surface, such as a bevel or cylinder. Terrain: an editable mesh surface that can be sculpted, colored, split, or stitched.
Layer: a saved organization path for map objects. Group: a saved association of world brushes and terrain patches. Hidden or frozen items may be unavailable for selection.

sections.title: Appearance and collision
paragraphs: Material: the named asset applied to a surface. The browser's active material is used for new geometry and can be applied to selected surfaces.
Projection or UV alignment: the shift, repeat size, rotation, and skew that place a texture on a brush face.
Caulk: a material used on faces that should not render visibly. Auto Caulk targets fully covered coplanar faces between selected opaque brushes.
Alpha: a transparency or blend value used in terrain painting and overlays. A decal is a separate projected mesh clipped to its target brush face.
Collision: the geometry that blocks players or projectiles. Terrain mesh collision acts from its front side; use closed brushes for barriers that must block from both sides.

sections.title: Files and previews
paragraphs: .map: the editable Radiant source document. Save it to preserve changes.
.d3dbsp: a compiled map build that can be opened as a read-only preview.
.ff: a fastfile build output, separate from the editable .map source.
.lin: a leak path diagnostic that can be overlaid through View > Import leak path.

steps.title: Choose the right document
steps.text: Open a .map through File > Open .map… to edit. If you opened a .d3dbsp preview, return to the source .map before trying to change geometry.

tips: If an object is absent after loading a .map, check the open status for preserved unsupported primitives and check layer or filter visibility before assuming it was deleted.
